newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close lower as high-tech rise fades.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close lower as high-tech rise fades.

text.p: Taiwan share prices lost their early gains and tailed off in late trade to end lower on Thursday, with profit-taking erasing gains even in recently hot electronics, brokers said.
The weighted index reached an intra-day high of 8,127.16 points but suffered a wave of late selling to finish 60.81 points or 0.75 percent lower at 7,997.65.
Turnover was a moderately active T$110.17 billion.
The index had opened higher with investors hunting for bargains after the market's consecutive losses on Tuesday and Wednesday.
Buying interest dissipated in late trade, returning the market to what some brokers predicted would be a long, gradual descent to support around 7,800.
"It was obvious from today's session that the market was incapable of sustaining a significant rise," said Oliver Fang, senior analyst for National Securities.

The bedrock electronics sector, which had been rejuvenated in recent days while tracking gains by high-tech shares on Wall Street, rose as much as 3.26 percent early in the session but finished with only a modest 0.32 percent gain.
"The rest of the market had been supported by electronics, and once electronics started to slow the index could not find other support," Fang said.

The market, beset by political jitters and concerns over social disorder, has been mired in a low-turnover consolidation for more than a month, struggling to rekindle the kind of sustained rally seen earlier in the year. Some analysts warn that stocks had become overvalued in the long bull run that drove the index to a six-year peak 8,661.72 on April 26.
As in previous days, Thursday's focus was heavily on electronics, which fielded the five most traded shares.
